name: Sony PlayStation 2 family
summary: Explore PS2 fat and slim hardware and homebrew entry points: FreeMcBoot on memory card or hard drive for fat models, and FreeDVDBoot on all slims.

specs.memory: 32 MB RDRAM main memory + 4 MB embedded video memory
specs.storage: 8 MB memory card; hard drive in the fat models' expansion bay

variants.storage: Internal HDD via expansion bay (network adapter required)
variants.notes: SCPH-10000 through SCPH-55000 and SCPH-3000x/3500x/37000/390xx groups. Expansion bay for a hard drive and network adapter; early 10000-series use a PC-card-style expansion.

variants.storage: No internal HDD; 8 MB memory card
variants.notes: SCPH-700xx through 900xx groups. Internal power supply, no expansion bay; Ethernet built in.

firmware.version: N/A (BIOS fixed per model; no online updates)

homebrew.name: FreeMcBoot / FreeHDBoot (FMCB/FHDB)
homebrew.firmware: Every model; memory-card route works on all PS2; hard-drive route requires a fat model with network adapter and HDD
homebrew.summary: An installer that puts a boot loader on a memory card (FMCB) or on a hard drive (FHDB), so homebrew starts with the console. The installer is freely available from the community.

compatibility.note: Memory-card boot works on all PS2 models. The installer version current on psdevwiki is v1.9x, upgraded from the original v1.8C.
Hard-drive booting (FHDB) requires the network adapter and an installed HDD; slims have no expansion bay.

requirements: A memory card for FMCB; or a network adapter and IDE HDD for FHDB (fat models only).
warnings: Memory cards are old; failing cards can corrupt the FMCB install. Keep a spare card and a backup of the FMCB install.

homebrew.name: FreeDVDBoot
homebrew.firmware: Slim: all models supported; fat: version-specific (DVD Player versions 2.10, 2.12, 3.04; Sony patched the exploit in 2.14)
homebrew.summary: A DVD-player exploit that lets a burned DVD boot homebrew on an unmodified console. All PS2 Slim and Bravia TV units are supported per upstream; a phat needs the ISO matching its DVD Player version.

compatibility.note: Upstream states every PS2 Slim and Bravia TV unit is supported, with no per-version ISO needed.
Upstream lists DVD Player versions 2.10, 2.12 and 3.04 as supported on fat models, with a note that Sony patched the exploit in 2.14.

requirements: A DVD drive on the console and a computer with a disc burner.
Console language set to English (the exploit is language-dependent).
A DVD-R disc; rewritable media puts more strain on the laser.
warnings: Burn at the lowest speed and finalise the disc; failing to do so may cause read errors.
Console must be set to English language; other languages change memory contents and break the exploit.
